### ① Derived judgments

**1. One stamp, one derivation — RIGHT.** `unmaskedColumnKeysKey` is `JSON.stringify` of the keys of `tableColumns` entries with `col.masked !== true`, keyed on `[tableColumns]` alone; `tableColumns` is the one place that stamps `masked` (`objectTypesPending || isMaskedDetailFieldType(col.type, fieldDef?.type)`), so the withheld window and a masked type both reach the filter and the sort through the same stamp. The only added non-comment source line in `RelatedList.tsx` that mentions a masked token is `col.masked === true` — a read of the stamp, not a restatement; neither `isMaskedDetailFieldType`, `isMaskedFieldType`, `'password'`, `'secret'` nor `objectTypesPending` appears in any added code line of the filter or sort. The key is content (a string), so `filteredData` `[relatedData, filterText, windowed, unmaskedColumnKeysKey]`, `sortedData` `[…, unmaskedColumnKeysKey]`, `handleSort` `[sortField, unmaskedColumnKeysKey]` and `handleTableSort` `[unmaskedColumnKeysKey]` re-run on a set change and not on a recomputed `tableColumns` identity — the `expandKey` / `selectKey` pattern commandment #10 asks for. Key spelling matches the stamp's: `drawnColumnKey` is `accessorKey || columnIdentity`, the same expression `tableColumns` and the button row use. `readColumnKeys` is a plain `JSON.parse`; `unmaskedColumnKeys` is re-parsed each render and used only in JSX, never as a dependency.

**2. Filter — RIGHT.** Head `filteredData` sweeps `readColumnKeys(unmaskedColumnKeysKey)` reading `row?.[key]` raw. `data-table`'s own search at `origin/main` is `columns.filter((col) ⇒ !isMaskedColumnKey(rawColumns, col.accessorKey))` over `row[col.accessorKey]` raw: the displayed columns minus the masked ones, raw values — the same rule. The narrowing is stated in the changeset as its own paragraph ("Narrowing, stated: … a term that matches only a field no column shows no longer keeps a row") and in the README hunk ("a field no column shows, never keeps a row"), and pinned (`ECHO`, an undeclared row key; `TOKEN-C`, a declared `secret` the authored columns omit). Column shapes: a bare string is normalized by `effectiveColumns`' `normalizeColumn` to `{ accessorKey: c, header, fieldDef, fieldType }` before any stamp, so it is an object at `tableColumns` (pinned as the first shape); an authored object resolves through `accessorKey || columnIdentity`; a column with an author `cell` is searched on `row[key]` exactly as the table searches it, and if its type is masked it is stamped regardless of the `cell` so it is excluded; a reference column is searched on its raw id (or `[object Object]` for an expanded row) — the same as before this PR and the same as the table, so the sweep neither newly misses what the user sees nor searches a hidden value. A column dropped by FLS or the parent key is not in `tableColumns`, so its row value is no longer swept — part of the stated narrowing and a leak the old `Object.values(row)` had. A non-object entry, which `tableColumns` passes through unstamped, is excluded by the `typeof col !== 'object'` guard: fail closed.

**3. Sort — RIGHT for the card's named sites.** The `list` card's button row returns `null` when `!unmaskedColumnKeys.includes(field)`, after the existing `windowed && withheldFromServerSort` check; `handleSort` and `handleTableSort` both `return` before any `setSortField` when the key is not in the unmasked set; `sortedData` returns `filteredData` unchanged when `sortField` is not an unmasked column; `setSortField` has exactly two call sites, both guarded, so in windowed mode a user sort on a column already stamped never reaches `fetchSortField` (pinned: `onSortChange([{ field: 'api_key' … }])` sends no `$orderby`, `name desc` does). The authored `defaultSort` on a masked field going out as `$orderby`: the card names the filter sweep, the `list` card's sort buttons and `sortedData` ordering by `row[sortField]`; `defaultSort` never sets `sortField` and never enters `sortedData` (the existing `RelatedList.sortDroppedOutsideWindowed` header says so and its CONTROL pins the `$orderby`), so it is a third path the card does not name. The spec header at objectstack `origin/main` says of `encrypted` / `secret` that "neither door refuses an ORDER BY over one" and "if any of them should be refused, that is a runtime-door decision first". Leaving it, and reporting it as a finding, is consistent with the card's scope and with AGENTS.md #0.1 (fix it at the producer or the door, not with a renderer-side rule restated at the fetch).

**4. Moved block — RIGHT; the residual is CONFIRMED and reachable only by a prop change on a mounted list.** The hook sequence of base and head differ only by the six moved hooks (`filteredData`, `sortedData`, the page-reset effect, `handleSort`, `activeSort`, `handleTableSort`) relocating past eight non-effect hooks (`deleteTarget` state, `handleDeleteRow`, `handleConfirmDelete`, `handleAddRecords`, `effectiveColumns`, `withheldFromServerSort`, `sortableColumns`, `tableColumns`) plus the new `unmaskedColumnKeysKey` memo; no hook is conditional; the one moved effect still runs after every fetch effect and before `useIsMobile`, so effect order is unchanged. Nothing between the old and new position reads a moved identifier (two comment mentions only). The windowed fetch's inputs — `fetchPage`, `fetchSortField`, `fetchSortDirection`, `defaultSortKey`, `filterKey`, `expandKey`, `selectKey`, `objectSchemaReady` — are computed before the fetch effect and are not in the diff. Residual: the fetch builds `const orderby = fetchSortField ? [{ field: fetchSortField, order: fetchSortDirection }] : defaultSortSpec` with no masked check, and `sortField` is never cleared (no `setSortField(null)` anywhere, none on an `api` change), so a user sort set while its column was unmasked and stamped LATER is sent as `$orderby`, and in client mode `activeSort` still names it on the table's headers. Reachable only when the stamp lands after the sort: `columns` re-typed or `api` switched on a mounted list, i.e. a direct React consumer of the exported component. Through `record:related_list` (`columns` and `api` static per node, and both setters refusing every key while `objectTypesPending` holds) it is not reachable.

**5. Pins — RIGHT.** Twelve cases, no `.skip`, `.only`, `.todo` or timeout in the file.
